```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,

source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab08", title = "Residuals Analysis")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Good forecast residuals should look approximately like:",
  q2 = "Leftover seasonal spikes in residual ACF usually mean:",
  q3 = "Which model has residuals closer to white noise for Beer, and why?"

```

## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Fit and residual plots
```{r resid-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=14}
library(fpp3)
fits <- aus_production |>
  model(
    ses = ETS(Beer ~ error("A") + trend("N") + season("N")),
    snaive = SNAIVE(Beer)
  )
fits |> select(ses) |> gg_tsresiduals()
fits |> select(snaive) |> gg_tsresiduals()
augment(fits) |> features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 8)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("White noise (uncorrelated, mean near 0)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("A random walk"),
  answer("A strong seasonal pattern"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Seasonality was not fully captured", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The model is perfect"),
  answer("You must never use SNAIVE"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Prefer … because residual ACF / Ljung–Box …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```
